candidate.title: snmC-Seq
candidate.scope: The middle snmC-Seq row of the assigned Illumina diagram: single-nucleus methylcytosine sequencing through lysis, bisulfite conversion, adapter-bearing random priming, extension, pooled Adaptase processing, and amplification/sequencing. Luo et al. (2017; PMID 28798132) establishes the named nucleus-based assay and its combined 5mC/5hmC measurement. snmC-seq in that paper is the same method name with different capitalization. The independent Duplex-Seq and scAba-Seq rows are neighboring context, not alternatives or connected branches of this assigned card. The left methylated-strand icon illustrates the target, not a separate transfer operation. This record captures the schematic architecture, not a complete experimental implementation.

operations.label: Bisulfite conversion
operations.description: Apply the depicted bisulfite treatment to released genomic DNA, yielding the converted DNA template used for random priming.
operations.mechanism: Bisulfite conversion is named in the drawing; the inspected main text establishes that its modification-sensitive readout combines 5mC and 5hmC. The conversion chemistry is not expanded into unshown steps.

operations.label: Random priming
operations.description: Associate the random-primer portion of an adapter-bearing primer with the bisulfite-converted DNA template. The output is a primed template, before the separately drawn extension.
operations.mechanism: The short green primer is drawn aligned to the blue template and joined to an orange adapter segment.
operations.information_effect: Places the adapter-bearing primer at an initiation site for copying the converted DNA. The diagram does not identify the primer as a unique molecular tag or a cell barcode.

operations.label: Extend
operations.description: Extend the annealed primer along the converted template, producing a longer DNA copy carrying the primer-associated adapter.
operations.mechanism: Primer extension is depicted by the short priming segment becoming a long complementary strand. No particular polymerase is named.
operations.information_effect: Carries the converted genomic sequence into adapter-bearing DNA products. Products remain in separate sample preparations until the following pooling step.

operations.label: Pool samples and Adaptase reaction
operations.description: Mix the independently prepared extended DNA products and carry out the combined, named Adaptase processing block; the output is the mixed set of inserts shown with colored terminal segments.
operations.mechanism: Kept at the single combined block shown: the drawing does not resolve the order or molecular intermediates within pooling and Adaptase processing.
operations.information_effect: Combines DNA products from multiple samples in one pool. Colored ends are retained as depicted adapter-associated structure; their exact sample-index meaning is unresolved in the inspected evidence.

evidence.locator: Middle row: rightward arrow from Extend to multiple parallel blue inserts with colored ends, caption Pool samples and Adaptase reaction.

operations.label: Amplify and sequence
operations.description: Amplify the pooled library products to produce the sequencing DNA library and sequence this DNA, yielding the snmC-Seq sequence readout. The two actions remain one operation at the resolution of the source caption.
operations.information_effect: Reads the DNA copies of bisulfite-treated genomic templates to support covered-region methylcytosine profiles. The original cytosine modification is inferred from this sequence readout rather than directly chemically measured in the final library; 5mC and 5hmC remain combined. The small colored mark in the final icon is not labeled as a mutation in this row.
